subject: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exception backlog — roadmap asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exceptions — need a canonical rubric

Team —

We have three concurrent asks from MedServe (audit evidence for a recent SOC2 request), a partner onboarding that needs a permanent SSO exemption for service accounts, and a handful of older retention carveouts tracked as ad-hoc spreadsheets. Rather than continue triaging case-by-case, I want to establish a single rubric and roadmap workstream so we can: 

- Capture current outstanding carveouts with minimal fields (reason, duration, owner, evidence location)
- Define guardrails for permanent vs timeboxed exceptions
- Decide if BYOK/KMS work or audit-log retention enhancements are required to close the largest 30-day evidence requests

Attached: retention-exemptions.csv (current inventory), sso-exceptions-inventory.xlsx, initial-scope-notes.pdf

Asks: please reply with (a) product impact / feature asks, (b) security constraints, (c) rough engineering estimate and can we commit to a Q1 2027 delivery for the minimal rubric + doc?

Goal: ship a small PRD + enforcement checklist by Dec 8 so sales/CS can stop re-running manual packaging for each case.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exceptions — need a canonical rubric

Jonas —

Thanks for the consolidation. From Product POV: 

- Minimal product surface to unblock the top 20 carriers: a tenant-level retention-override flag (timeboxed, enforced via policy in Console) + audit-log export window extension API. That would close ~60% of current requests.
- BYOK ask: customers want an option to provide keys for long-term escrow of audit exports. That is larger scope — likely a multi-quarter effort (design + KMS integration).
- SSO service-account exemptions: this is mostly an ops workflow problem; a small Console flow to register a service account + attach an exception ticket should be sufficient.

Impact / constraints: must be audited (traceability), and any Console change needs an admin approval flow. I created a starter Jira SUP-4321 and dropped a rough PRD link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4321 and https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDeF-retention-rubric

Estimate (very rough):
- Retention-override flag + export window API: 4-6 wk engineering (1 backend, 1 infra, 0.5 frontend) for MVP + tests
- Console exception flow: 2-3 wk
- BYOK for audit export: exploratory + security design 4-6 wk, follow-on implementation TBD

If the ask is Q1, we can do the two small items in a single sprint cycle across teams if infra prioritizes the export API.

— Karthik
Product Manager, Platform
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-26T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exceptions — need a canonical rubric

Quick notes from Security: 

- Any retention-override needs immutable evidence (signed manifest + access log) and must appear in the audit trail. We cannot accept silent server-side retention changes without traceability.
- BYOK for audit export is acceptable but must integrate with our KMS policy and HSM requirements for key usage logs — that will require significant legal/compliance review for customers that ask for escrow.
- For MedServe: they want retention evidence for a 90-day window + SSO exception for a set of CI/CD service accounts. We can provide a packaged evidence export, but if the exemption is permanent we need an approval workflow and a compensating control (narrowed scope, IP allowlist).

Request: Priyom, can infra/ops provide an implementation sketch for the audit export (format, retention boundary, signed artifacts) and a runbook for on-demand evidence packaging? If we can produce a template by next Tue (12/1), we can unblock the immediate MedServe ask.

— Neha
Head of Security Engineering
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exceptions — need a canonical rubric

On Fri, Nov 26, 2026 at 02:18 PM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick notes from Security: 
> 
> - Any retention-override needs immutable evidence (signed manifest + access log) and must appear in the audit trail.

Agreed — implementation sketch below: 

- Audit export format: gzipped JSONL containing event stream + manifest.json with SHA256 + signature via a dedicated key.
- Retention boundary: export API accepts start/end and a reason code; exports are stored in a timeboxed S3 bucket with lifecycle rule 365d unless BYOK escrow requested.
- Signed artifacts: use a service signing key rotated monthly, entries logged to audit-stream.
- Runbook: a short script (internal) to assemble evidence + verify signatures; we can template this and hand it to CS.

Estimate: core export API + storage lifecycle + runbook — 3-4 weeks with one infra engineer and one backend. BYOK escrow integration: additional 6+ wks.

I will drop an RFC in the infra repo and link to the PR in SUP-4321 by EOD Monday.

— Priyom
Staff Engineer, Infrastructure
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lang <thomas.lang@medservehealth.com>, medserve-security@medservehealth.com
Date: 2026-11-29T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate audit retention carveouts + SSO exceptions — need a canonical rubric

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

- Short-term (blockers): Priyom to produce the export + runbook template by 2026-12-01. This will be used to create the MedServe evidence package in the next 48 hours.
- Product MVP: Karthik to own SUP-4321; retention-override flag + export window API + console exception flow targeted for a Q1 ship (tentative sprint in Jan).
- Security guardrails: Neha to produce the approval checklist and required metadata for any exception (signed manifest, scope, owner, compensating controls).
- BYOK: defer to design track; Neha + Karthik to scope customer-facing requirements and legal/regulatory considerations — tentative kickoff 2027-01-10.

Meeting: 2026-12-02 10:00 AM PT for a 30-min sync (calendar invite sent). Please add any missing items in SUP-4321.

Jonas
Director, Security & Compliance
